_meta.region: Northern Kazakhstan grain belt (Kostanay, Akmola, North Kazakhstan)
_meta.status: DRAFT for agronomist review. Keys ending in _j are the drafter's own judgement, not a sourced number.
_meta.scales: 1 = poor/low, 5 = good/high. water_use_j: 1 = leaves most water for the next crop, 5 = dries the profile.

sources.FAO_T6_T14: https://www.fao.org/4/s2022e/s2022e07.htm (FAO Irrigation Water Management Training Manual 3: Table 6 growing period, Table 14 crop water need; values are for unstressed, irrigated crops)
sources.FAO56_T22: https://www.fao.org/4/x0490e/x0490e0e.htm (FAO-56 Table 22 maximum effective rooting depth)
sources.ALBERTA_GM: https://www1.agric.gov.ab.ca/$department/deptdocs.nsf/all/faq7979 (N fixed under irrigation, lb N/ac; converted x1.12)
sources.AREA_2025: https://agroreview.com/en/newsen/crops/kazakhstan-increased-production-oilseeds-and/ (2025 areas, secondary report of Bureau of National Statistics data)

crops.name: Spring wheat (bread)
crops.frost_seedling: tolerant to about -6 C until the 5-leaf stage (growing point below ground)
crops.market_reason: About 12 Mha, elevators everywhere, state FCC floor purchase (class 3: 115,000 KZT/t, Oct 2025), buyers Uzbekistan, Afghanistan, Tajikistan. Low price (65-70k KZT/t early 2025) and rail bottlenecks are the reason government wants less of it.

crops.name: Durum wheat
crops.market_reason: Niche premium crop (about 0.8 Mt in 2025). Italy is a regular buyer of Kazakh wheat. Quality discounts are severe after a wet harvest (vitreousness, sprouting), and FCC pays only 90,000 KZT/t.
crops.yield_note: judgement: no separate national series, assumed close to bread wheat
crops.source: FAO_T6_T14; FAO56_T22; FAS March 2026 update (FCC price table)

crops.name: Spring barley
crops.market_reason: Feed demand is growing (livestock, feed-flour exports to China), exports 1.6-2.1 Mt a year to Iran, China, Uzbekistan. FCC buys class 2 at 75,000 KZT/t. Iran route disrupted in 2025-26.

crops.name: Oats
crops.frost_seedling: tolerant, but growing point is more exposed than wheat at emergence
crops.market_reason: Small crop (about 0.18-0.24 Mha), mostly used on farm as feed. Best-documented local replacement for bare fallow.
crops.yield_note: national 2015-2024; Barayev 20-year mean 2.38 t/ha when grown in place of fallow

crops.name: Oilseed flax (linseed)
crops.frost_seedling: tolerates to about -8 C once past the 2-leaf stage and hardened; emerging seedlings are tender
crops.market_reason: 1.35 Mha and 1.35 Mt in 2025 (+54% area). Export crop to the EU and China at 200,000 KZT/t or more in 2025. Volatile: area fell to 0.73 Mha in 2023 after prices dropped.
crops.source: FAO_T6_T14 (days only); FAO56_T22; FAOSTAT; BARAYEV_DIV; AREA_2025

crops.name: Sunflower (early hybrids)
crops.frost_seedling: cotyledon stage fairly hardy; -1 to -2 C at bud or flowering damages heads, so a September frost on a late crop is the real risk
crops.market_reason: Largest oilseed: 1.78 Mha, 2.46 Mt in 2025, domestic crushers, China takes about 80% of seed exports. Export duty of 20% (min 100 EUR/t) pushes seed to local processors; a per-tonne subsidy for delivery to processors is reported.
crops.yield_note: national 2015-2024; Barayev 10-year mean 0.70 in the dry steppe

crops.name: Spring rapeseed (canola)
crops.frost_seedling: hardened seedlings survive -8 C or lower; unhardened seedlings after a warm spell die at -3 to -4 C
crops.market_reason: Fastest-growing oilseed: 0.32 Mha in 2025 (+117%), USDA puts 2026 at 0.49 Mha and 0.84 Mt. Price 200,000 KZT/t or more. Fits the wetter forest-steppe (North Kazakhstan, northern Akmola), not the dry steppe.
crops.yield_note: national 2015-2025; Barayev 10-year mean only 0.67 at Shortandy

crops.name: Lentil
crops.frost_seedling: cold tolerant, sown at 5 C soil; can regrow from below-ground nodes
crops.n_fix_note: dryland range is judgement; 150 kg/ha measured under irrigation
crops.market_reason: Boom crop: 0.64 Mha and about 0.78 Mt in 2025 (+83% area). Turkey takes close to 90% of exports, so prices fell on oversupply. Seed subsidised (239,300 KZT/t for original seed).
crops.source: FAO_T6_T14 (days only); FAO56_T22; FAOSTAT; ALBERTA_GM; BARAYEV_DIV; FAS_2026; AREA_2025

crops.name: Field pea
crops.frost_seedling: cold tolerant, sown at 5 C soil; regrows from scale nodes after frost
crops.n_fix_note: dryland range is judgement; 200 kg/ha measured under irrigation
crops.market_reason: About 0.11-0.15 Mha. A new deep-processing plant (KazProtein) plans to take 80,000 t of peas a year. Thinner buyer network than lentil.
crops.source: FAO_T6_T14; FAO56_T22; FAOSTAT; ALBERTA_GM; BARAYEV_DIV; FAS_2026

crops.name: Chickpea
crops.frost_seedling: desi types germinate at 5 C, kabuli needs 10 C; late maturity exposes green pods to September frost
crops.n_fix_note: dryland range is judgement; 121 kg/ha measured under irrigation; needs its own inoculant strain
crops.market_reason: Tiny crop (8,000-24,000 ha nationally), few buyers and little local seed. Barayev zoning recommends it for the driest southern districts of Akmola.

crops.name: Proso millet
crops.frost_seedling: none: killed by frost, sown late May to early June into warm soil
crops.market_reason: 25,000-61,000 ha, small domestic groats and feed market. Insurance crop: in the 2012 drought it out-yielded wheat by 0.3 t/ha at Shortandy.

crops.name: Sweet clover green manure (undersown, ploughed down in year 2)
crops.season_days_local_j: biennial: undersown in a cereal, terminated June-July of the fallow year
crops.n_fix_note: dryland range is judgement; 250 kg/ha measured under irrigation
crops.market_reason: No grain to sell: the return is nitrogen, soil cover and forage or honey. Uses more soil water than other green manures, which has suppressed the next crop in dry years (Alberta Agriculture).
crops.yield_note: wheat after sweet clover ploughdown averaged 1.96 t/ha over 13 years (Barayev)

predecessor_yield_factor._note: Yield of the following wheat relative to wheat after bare fallow = 1.00.
predecessor_yield_factor._sources: fallow/oats/lentil/mustard: Barayev poster 2018-2020 (21.4, 20.1, 18.8-18.9 c/ha). field_pea: Suleimenov et al. 2005 (fallow advantage 20-25% over oats and dry pea). second wheat: USDA IPAD 2009 (15-20% drop). Keys ending _j are judgement.
